chunks: And Moses said: "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."
ai.seo_question: What did Moses say to Pharaoh when he was sent as a messenger?
ai.summary: In the context of the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, this verse underscores the divine mandate of prophethood against earthly tyranny, a theme central to Shia exegesis regarding the legitimacy of the Imams as inheritors of prophetic authority. The declaration 'Lord of the worlds' (Rabb al-Alamin) emphasizes God's universal sovereignty, contrasting with Pharaoh's claim to divinity, thereby establishing the theological basis for monotheistic resistance. This moment is often cited in Shia scholarship to illustrate the clarity of prophetic mission and the inevitability of divine justice over oppressive rulers.
